## opencode {VERSION}

{Prerelease/Stable} release from `{branch}` branch. This maintenance release focuses on cancellation, safe recovery from incomplete model responses, and actionable diagnostics.

---

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Cancel pending asynchronous Stop callbacks**: Session abort invalidates the cancelled task's pending hook continuation. Admission checks prevent an old callback from starting a new model turn after cancellation. Normal callbacks and later user requests retain their existing behavior (#774).
- **Recover incomplete responses before tool execution**: Incomplete tool input enters the existing finite retry path only when no tool has executed or may have executed. Failed attempts are isolated, and retry exhaustion retains an explicit error. Cancellation, permission rejection, and possibly completed tool side effects do not authorize replay (#773).
- **Recover missing answers and interrupted requests safely**: Empty conversation attempts and abnormally ended reasoning-only attempts use the existing finite retry budget and report an explicit error after exhaustion. Normally completed reasoning-only responses remain valid. Recognized transient errors can retry after partial text or reasoning, while an unknown finish alone does not establish a network failure. Every retry checks whether a tool executed or may have executed before replaying a request (#778).
- **Explain Grep and Glob filesystem failures**: Missing paths, filesystem access denial, invalid path components, and traversal failures retain the resolved path and useful error category. Failed searches do not silently broaden their scope or report partial output as complete. Agent-policy checks remain separate (#772, #776).
- **Preserve custom-model long-context pricing**: Configured `cost.context_over_200k` reaches runtime pricing metadata. Existing pricing precedence and normalized-token threshold behavior are preserved. This affects local estimates, not provider billing or context limits (#764).
- **Give action-specific workflow authoring guidance**: Start, extend, and replan diagnostics explain their own accepted envelopes. Draft output is explicitly a start document. Strict validation and workflow recovery policy are unchanged (#775).
- **Retain DAG child error identity**: Live failure handling and recovery keep the persisted assistant error name without copying provider or tool payloads. Interrupted children report that their interruption source is unknown and advise checking side effects before manual recovery. Failure classification and cancellation policy are unchanged; this is a partial diagnostic fix, not resolution of the original interruption investigation (#777).

### 🔍 Verification

**Open investigations:**

- **Claude signed thinking replay (#768)** remains open. No automatic beta opt-in, blanket reasoning removal, or account-specific acceptance is claimed. The audit distinguishes client history changes from opaque upstream routing and account facts.
- **DAG worker interruption (#777)** remains an investigation. A rejected tool call followed by an interrupted model turn does not establish that the rejection caused the interruption. No unrequested restart or replay of possibly completed side effects is introduced.

Focused regressions use isolated sessions and synthetic fixtures. They do not establish the behavior of an opaque provider relay or a production Claude/AWS account. Headless HTTP cancellation evidence does not, by itself, certify every graphical or terminal client cancellation path.

Installed-host acceptance passed 13 HTTP and 2 direct CLI cases for response recovery, plus normal asynchronous callback delivery and idle-session cancellation. The verified local test build was `1.0.76-local.20261013.2`; build and installed SHA-256 matched `4247e01ecca4e73fef489e722d2c8183876dabb69afae2f9fcdb9f1f94158b35`. Two harness readiness races were corrected and their affected cases rerun successfully; the original failed reports remain preserved. A separate probe could not establish tool execution before the same stream disconnected and is not counted as passing; that execution fence is covered by regressions and independent source review. Source/file stream classification is covered by adapter and processor regressions because the OpenAI-compatible host fixture cannot emit those SDK events.

CI review repairs also synchronize callback tests on actual discard signals and align CLI/parameter expectations with recovery and authoring behavior. The first full core review run encountered an existing process-readiness file race; its focused 23-test rerun and the final full core rerun passed.

The affected opencode and core package typechecks pass, as does the workspace typecheck (31 tasks). Root lint reports 4738 warnings and no errors against the unchanged 4750-warning cap. The DAG gate also verifies that generated SDK output has no drift.
